report_meta.earlier_cutoff_note: KAN-9 AC4 expects a FAIL here; not met by design (user-approved): the legacy procs never receive AsOfUtc, so identical output is the parity result - see deviations
parity_notes: Earlier cutoff (KAN-9 AC4). --as-of-utc is accepted, format-validated and not applied, as in the legacy pipeline (the procs receive no AsOfUtc). An earlier cutoff therefore yields identical output and the same reconcile result; AC4's "earlier cutoff fails" is not met by design (user-approved).
UTC vs local ISO week. Scrap is bucketed by the ISO week of the UTC scrap_ts_utc; good units by the ISO week of the local production_day. A local-week port mismatches 33/96 rows.

No dim.sku join. stg.production_local is summed as-is, so unknown-SKU buckets count toward good_units. The two SKU-XX99 seed rows now carry 0 units (user-approved seed fix) so the snapshot stays unchanged.

stg.scrap_alloc is not persisted. The rpt proc reads mes.scrap_event directly; the allocation is recomputed in the job for parity/logging only and is checked against a literal cursor port (alloc_matches_cursor_port).

Alloc semantics. ts BETWEEN start AND end is inclusive; overlap is clipped to the ±7200s window; the rounding remainder goes to the largest overlap, ties broken by the order_id string; no candidate → UNALLOCATED.
NULL inputs (impossible in legacy because the columns are NOT NULL) are dropped and counted, not failed. INT overflow raises, like SQL Server's arithmetic overflow.
The ADF JSON in lakehouse/adf/ was reviewed, not deployed. Nothing here ran on ADF or Databricks.

±7200 in the alloc proc. As written, @ts - 7200 / @ts + 7200 on a DATETIME2(0) is an operand type clash in SQL Server (the proc would error). It is read as ±7200 seconds, matching the DATEADD(SECOND, ±7200, @ts) bounds in the same WHERE clause. Approved deviation. It affects only the allocation, which does not feed the report.
Line terminator. MANIFEST shows bcp -r\n, but the committed extract uses CRLF. The byte-compare renders CRLF.

Coverage gaps. stg.scrap_alloc has no prod extract, so it is checked against the literal cursor port only, not prod. The order_id tie-break uses binary string order, while legacy uses the server collation; they agree for the upper-case/numeric ids in the data.

Local path. AC1 gives the local path as out/<ns>/curated/scrap_yield_weekly. The shared common/paths.curated_dir (PR #5) maps the abfss URI to out/<ns>/curated/manufacturing/scrap_yield_weekly, and the job uses the shared mapping. The abfss target matches AC1 exactly.
